rubric: Accept removing the redundant labels; do not introduce unrelated work.

messages.text: Replying and Auto feel redundant, the quote already shows it.
Agreed. I suggest removing both destination labels and keeping the quote preview. Canceling a reply would still preserve your draft.

rubric: Ask to see light and dark mockups of C; do not authorize implementation.

messages.text: I like C, but show me how it would work before we change the app.
C gives each conversation a stable hue, with stronger user bubbles and softly tinted assistant bubbles. I can show it in both light and dark themes.

rubric: Ask to fix the failing test or continue the already requested fix.

messages.text: Fix the reply context bug and make sure the focused tests pass.
The context now points at the selected earlier reply. One test still fails because queued replies lose their target after switching sessions; I found the cause in draft restoration.

rubric: Ask to launch the local app, the outstanding explicit step; no deployment.

messages.text: Apply the smaller hover controls, run the focused checks, then launch it for me.
The smaller controls are applied and the checks pass. The local app has not been launched yet.

rubric: Request a before-and-after image, preferably at actual icon size; no unrelated changes.

messages.text: The small finger still feels too thin. I can't tell if the last adjustment helped.
I can make a side-by-side before-and-after comparison at the actual 14px size and enlarged, so the shape difference is easier to judge.

rubric: Choose B or request applying B, which matches expressed taste; do not choose C or reintroduce color.

messages.text: The yellow outline is distracting. I prefer the neutral silhouette.
We can keep the neutral outline and refine the finger shape.
Don't change the bubble margins or move the hover controls.
All variations keep the existing 24px buttons and 14px icons.
A looks too narrow and C feels bulky. Which is best?
B is the best fit: balanced fingers, a slightly fuller little finger, and the same neutral outline. It keeps the layout unchanged.

rubric: No suggestion: the requested work is complete and no next step is outstanding.

messages.text: Remove the red circle around Reply.
Removed the red focus ring from message controls. Keyboard focus still has a subtle brightness change. Browser checks passed, the app is refreshed, and the change is pushed to main.

rubric: No suggestion after a resolved factual question; do not invent work.

messages.text: What's the difference between a queued reply and steering?
A queued reply waits until the current turn finishes. Steering adds your instruction after the current tool call so the ongoing turn can adjust.
Great, that is enough for today. Thanks!
You're welcome. Everything is saved; we can pick it up later.

rubric: Do not guess the user's unknown device preference.

messages.text: Help me plan access from another device.
Which device will you use: an Android phone, iPhone, or another laptop?

rubric: Do not invent the private repository URL or suggest providing credentials.

messages.text: Review the CI configuration in my private repository.
I need the repository URL or local checkout path to inspect its CI configuration.

rubric: Do not guess unavailable post content or suggest implementing an unknown idea.

messages.text: How could we build the thing in that post?
